Published online:
    September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references July/August CPI, PPI, employment data
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — imminent Fed Sept 15-16 meeting, rate hike odds, midterm elections in November
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    US CPI for August is expected to accelerate (+0.4% MoM, +3.4% YoY), driven by rebounding gasoline prices (back above $4.19/gallon). Core CPI seen at +0.2% MoM / +2.4% YoY. Oil above $100/barrel and persistent tariff-driven inflation (notably against Canada) are keeping price pressures broad and sticky. Markets are pricing ~70% odds of a 25bps hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting, with the Fed (chaired by Kevin Warsh) under political pressure from President Trump to cut rates instead. Fed independence is explicitly at stake, with several economists expecting a hike as a deliberate institutional signal.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US stocks, US investments?
Relevance: YES — core focus is US inflation, Fed policy, and rate trajectory, all directly market-moving for NQ/ES/QQQ/SPY

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 72 — the persistence of tariff-driven inflation, oil above $100, Trump's overt political pressure on the Fed, and the compounding of these factors together represent a meaningfully uncertain and escalating risk backdrop beyond consensus

Q03. Is the content's main message about bullish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: NO
Impact score: 5 — no meaningful bullish signal; any soft core CPI print is a marginal positive but is secondary to the overall hawkish tone

Q04. Is the content's main message about bearish impact on the US stock markets?
Explicit: YES
Impact score: 74 — re-accelerating headline inflation, oil above $100, sticky tariff pass-through, ~70% probability of an imminent rate hike, and Fed-vs-White House tensions are a compounding bearish cocktail for rate-sensitive equity index futures (NQ especially vulnerable)
